stature_conditioning: Weak: registered male sternum-stature correlations are r = 0.46-0.64, so a 1.82 m adjustment is small and uncertain; population means are context, not a scaled target.
topology_rules: costal cartilage 1 joins the manubrium (synchondrosis), below the clavicular notch
costal cartilage 2 joins at the sternal angle, the manubriosternal junction
costal cartilages 3-6 join the sternal body
costal cartilage 7 joins at or near the xiphisternal junction
ribs 8-10 reach the sternum only through the costal margin (interchondral), ribs 11-12 not at all

specimen_layout_grade_D.reading: Rib 2 at 45.4 mm against the manubriosternal junction at 45.0 mm; all topology rules hold; left/right within 0.4 mm.

findings: Sternum stick 213.2 mm against 154.1 +/- 13.1 mm total male sternum including xiphoid (z 4.5).
Rib 2 attaches 38.7 mm below the top but the manubriosternal marker is 76.1 mm down: rib 2 is not at the sternal angle (topology rule 2 fails).
Manubriosternal depth 76.1 mm against male manubrium lengths 46-55.2 mm.
Sternocostal spacing is near-uniform (29.8-35.2 mm): a schematic layout, not anatomical.

a 1.82 m-conditioned sternal length (or an explicit population-mean policy given weak stature correlation)
